scope: Botanical research for CA-01 through CA-12 only. This file is an authoring aid; it does not change the app, existing native data, or Phase 0.
interpretation: Proposed heightIn is representative mature overall height, including flowers when they rise above foliage. Spread is mature garden width; spreading colonies can exceed it.

Space is proposed on-center design spacing, not a independently established biological constant. All grow values are approximate planning years to the represented woody size, not published age-to-maturity measurements.

Numeric USDA bands are cultivation screening ranges, not native ranges or guarantees of heat, humidity, or drainage suitability. Several upper endpoints remain explicitly provisional; do not mistake Sunset zones or occurrence-map zones for USDA cultivation evidence.
Bloom months are representative California windows, not local forecasts. Persistent dried flowers and seedheads are not additional bloom months.

Current app categories treat woody-based, regularly rejuvenated perennials as forb. Botanical subshrub qualifications are retained below; evergreen shrubs with a persistent woody framework remain shrub.
Lifespan is recorded qualitatively unless a source documents more. No unsupported numerical survival promise, deer resistance, or rabbit resistance is proposed.
CNPS Calscape pages returned 403 during this review. Accessible UC ANR, university arboreta, NRCS, CNPS chapters, AHS, and firsthand native-plant growers supplied the evidence.

ucDeer.supports: Garden size 4–5 ft high × 5–7 ft wide; June–July flowers; sun/part shade; moderate to very low irrigation.

usdaDeer.supports: Warm-season bunchgrass, approximately 5 ft in flower; basal tufts can reach 6 ft across. Good drainage; southwestern North American origin.

mbgDeer.supports: Header zones 6–9; discussion reports common nursery ranges 7–10 and uncertain cold-edge hardiness. September–November bloom differs from California observations.

cnpsGrass.supports: Deergrass is evergreen with sun/light-shade and low-water use.

ucNativeSale.supports: Purple needlegrass approximately 3 ft × 1.5 ft, March–May, full sun, hardy to 5°F. Hummingbird sage flowering stems 1–3 ft; runners, evergreen in suitable conditions.

usdaNeedle.supports: Purple needlegrass under Nassella pulchra; long-lived perennial bunchgrass useful in California restoration.

calfloraNeedle.supports: Stipa pulchra accepted; Nassella pulchra retained as alternative name. California/western North American origin.

ucNeedle.supports: Purple needlegrass foliage clumps approximately 1–2 ft wide; flowering stems 2–3 ft. Seasonal growth follows rainfall.

nrscFuchsia.supports: Epilobium canum is a rhizomatous herbaceous perennial/subshrub, 1–3 ft high, usually flowering August–October. Subspecies differ in geographic and elevational adaptation.

ucFuchsia.supports: Species/cultivar group spans 6 inches–4 ft high; spreads; sun/part shade and low water. Annual winter cutback. Very broad bloom window explicitly depends on cultivar.

cnpsSouth.supports: California fuchsia approximately 1–2 ft × 3+ ft; California buckwheat approximately 4 ft × 4+ ft; seaside daisy approximately 1 ft × 3 ft.

ahsFuchsia.supports: Planting-zone index lists Epilobium canum USDA 8–11; its second numeric pair is AHS heat zones, not USDA.

osuBuckwheat.supports: Evergreen low shrub; sun and well-drained gravelly conditions; hardy to USDA 7; flowers late spring into early fall.

growerBuckwheat.supports: Species garden dimensions approximately 3–4 ft high × 4–5 ft wide.

cnpsBuckwheat.supports: Evergreen California buckwheat tolerates dry conditions; aging coppery flower heads provide lasting structure.

ucCleveland.supports: Cleveland sage evergreen shrub, 3–5 ft high × 5–8 ft wide, full sun/little water, late spring–early summer flowers, cold tolerance reported to 20°F.

ucClevelandCold.supports: Cleveland sage approximately 3 ft with flower spikes above; hardy USDA 8 and above, spring flowering, low irrigation.

cnpsCleveland.supports: Southern California chaparral sage for dry sunny gardens; aromatic foliage.

ucPenstemon.supports: Foothill penstemon evergreen perennial, 1–3 ft, spring/summer flowering; drainage and restrained irrigation matter.

ohioPenstemon.supports: Variety heterophyllus is suffrutescent/woody based, described as long-lived; April–July flowers.

growerPenstemon.supports: Firsthand species cultivation: USDA 7–10; height 0.5–1 m, width 0.5–1.5 m; flower spikes approximately 3 ft, April–August. Sun, drainage, drought tolerance. Reports some parent plants exceeding 20 years but this is not a universal lifespan.

calfloraPenstemon.supports: Penstemon heterophyllus is accepted and California endemic; multiple botanical varieties.

ucMilkweed.supports: Narrowleaf milkweed 3 ft × 3 ft; June–September bloom; sun/part shade, moderate/low water, winter dormancy and spread by runners/seed.

ucMilkweedZones.supports: Narrowleaf milkweed listed with USDA 6–10, deciduous perennial, approximately 3 ft × 2 ft.

usdaMilkweed.supports: Asclepias fascicularis identity and western habitat; local-origin material advised. Milkweed ingestion can be toxic.

ucHummingbird.organization: UC ANR San Luis Obispo County
ucHummingbird.supports: Herbaceous spreading perennial, foliage 1–2 ft high × 3+ ft wide, March–June flowers; sun/part shade, drought tolerance and occasional irrigation. Reports 20°F hardiness.

cnpsHummingbird.supports: Semi-evergreen herbaceous hummingbird sage forms 1–2 ft mounds with taller spikes, can spread to 6 ft. Can become summer dormant without irrigation; dry-shade use.

ahsHummingbird.supports: Salvia spathacea listed USDA 8–11. Local California sources are preferable for flowering calendar.

ucSeaside.organization: UC ANR San Luis Obispo County
ucSeaside.supports: Seaside daisy 1 ft × 3 ft, spring/summer flowering with possible later repeat; full sun/light shade, burns in hot inland sun. Low water on coast, more inland. Cold tolerance reported to -5°F.

kpuSeaside.supports: Herbaceous perennial; flowers April–July, full sun and drainage. Height 0.2–0.4 m, spread 0.3–0.6 m; smaller dimensions than California garden source.

osuBlueblossom.supports: Evergreen upright shrub approximately 4–12 ft; USDA (7)8, occasional freeze damage in Corvallis; sun and drainage. Native California/Oregon.

ncBlueblossom.supports: Dimensions 4–14 ft high × 5–14 ft wide with larger unpruned plants discussed; rapid growth; mid-May–mid-June bloom. Zone listing 5–9 conflicts with OSU cold guidance and is not accepted wholesale here.

osuManzanita.supports: True species is low, prostrate evergreen shrub to approximately 2 ft, not the larger Howard McMinn stature; sun/light shade, drainage, USDA 7. Sonoma County restricted native origin.

growerManzanita.supports: Explicitly pure true species: typical 3 ft × 6 ft, winter pink/white flowers, evergreen, sun/light shade, occasional/no summer irrigation; best in native sandy soils.

osuHoward.supports: Exact cultivar independently measured 4–8 ft high × 6–10 ft wide; evergreen mounding habit; sun/light shade, USDA (6)7, long-lived in suitable sites.

ucHoward.supports: Exact Howard McMinn cultivar 4–6 ft × 5–7 ft; January–March bloom in Central Valley; more tolerant of moderate irrigation, shade, and clay than many manzanitas.

osuCoffeeberry.supports: Frangula californica, synonym Rhamnus californica; evergreen shrub/small tree, highly variable height; hardy USDA 7, sun/shade, limited to no irrigation.

cnpsCoffeeberry.supports: Coffeeberry approximately 8–10 ft × 4–8 ft; evergreen, April–July bloom; sun/light shade and occasional irrigation.

plants.name: Deergrass

botanical.persistence: Evergreen in mild California conditions; foliage may brown with cold or stress.

confidence.zones: medium: conservative overlap of conflicting published bands
confidence.bloomMonths: medium: California-local window conflicts with MBG fall calendar

caveats: Use UC Davis June–July as the representative California flowering window; do not mark persistent late-season seed stems as continuously flowering.
Warm-season classification follows NRCS; MBG calls it cool-season, an unresolved source discrepancy.
Allow space for a genuinely large clump. Good drainage matters more than the dry label alone.

plants.name: Purple Needlegrass

botanical.persistence: Cool wet-season growth; can turn dormant in the dry summer. Evergreen descriptions depend on water and climate.
botanical.lifespan: Long-lived perennial; no fixed lifespan proposed.

confidence.zones: low: cold threshold 5°F supports conservative whole-zone 8; upper 10 is provisional
confidence.bloomMonths: high for Santa Clara representative calendar

caveats: Do not confuse this native bunchgrass with existing Stipa/Nassella tenuissima.
The proposed zone band is incomplete evidence, not a verified nationwide suitability band.
Do not use the UC landscape list's numbered Sunset zones as USDA zones.

plants.name: California Fuchsia

botanical.growthForm: Rhizomatous herbaceous perennial/subshrub; some persistent woody basal tissue
botanical.woody: woody-based subshrub, not a large persistent woody framework
botanical.persistence: Perennial; tops can be winter dormant or semi-evergreen by site. Often cut back after bloom.
botanical.lifespan: Perennial colony; no fixed lifespan proposed.

confidence.dimensions: medium: species/subspecies variable, colony spread unbounded
confidence.bloomMonths: high for NRCS general species window

caveats: Forb follows the maintained-perennial app convention, while retaining the botanical subshrub qualification.
Do not import the June–January aggregate UC cultivar bloom window into a single straight-species record.
Do not transfer cold-hardiness of montane subspecies to unspecified lowland stock.

plants.name: California Buckwheat

botanical.persistence: Evergreen; dried rust-colored flower heads persist after bloom.
botanical.lifespan: Perennial shrub; no fixed lifespan proposed.

confidence.dimensions: high for a medium upright garden form
confidence.zones: medium-low: USDA lower 7 sourced; upper 10 provisional
confidence.bloomMonths: medium: translation of late spring–early fall

caveats: Growth forms differ among varieties and selections; this is not a prostrate cultivar.
Reserve the full woody spread. Dried flowers remain structure, not continuing fresh bloom.
Needs drainage; avoid assuming tolerance of humid, irrigated eastern gardens from USDA alone.

plants.name: Cleveland Sage

botanical.persistence: Evergreen to stress-thinned foliage; persistent woody stems.
botanical.lifespan: Perennial shrub; no fixed lifespan proposed.

confidence.zones: medium-low: conservative lower 9 from 20°F report; other UC source allows 8; upper 10 provisional

caveats: Flower stalks project above the rounded leafy framework; avoid rendering the entire plant as one solid flower dome.
Keep the species separate from interspecific Cleveland-sage hybrids.
Warm-season irrigation and drainage constraints are not expressed fully by the app moisture label.

plants.name: Foothill Penstemon

botanical.woody: woody base; conventionally grown as a flowering perennial
botanical.persistence: Perennial, evergreen or partly deciduous depending on site; sources differ.
botanical.lifespan: Can persist for many years in suitable dry sites; cultivar lifespan must not be generalized.

confidence.dimensions: medium: representative within a broad species range
confidence.bloomMonths: medium-high: April–July matches botanical variety account and lies within grower April–August

caveats: Forb follows the existing woody-based penstemon convention; retain the woody-base qualification in descriptions.
Drainage and avoidance of excess fertilizer/irrigation are central to persistence.
No Margarita BOP or other cultivar dimensions/hardiness were silently assigned to the straight species.

plants.name: Narrowleaf Milkweed

botanical.persistence: Winter dormant; foliage dies down and regrows from perennial roots.
botanical.lifespan: Perennial; colony spread by runners and seed.

confidence.zones: high for published UC cultivation band
confidence.bloomMonths: high for UC Davis representative calendar

caveats: Medium is a primary garden moisture setting; established plants also tolerate low water. This is not swamp milkweed.
Spread is a representative patch width, not a hard limit on runners.
Use locally appropriate nursery-grown material; milkweed sap/ingestion requires normal toxicity caution.

plants.name: Hummingbird Sage

botanical.growthForm: Rhizomatous herbaceous perennial sage, not a woody Cleveland-type shrub
botanical.persistence: Semi-evergreen; may become summer dormant without irrigation. Occasional water maintains foliage.
botanical.lifespan: Perennial spreading colony; no fixed lifespan proposed.

confidence.zones: medium: AHS 8–11 supports proposed subset; UC temperature thresholds conflict
confidence.bloomMonths: high for California primary local window

caveats: Do not classify all Salvia as shrubs; this species is herbaceous and spreading.
Dry partial shade is an important role, but complete summer dormancy can occur without supplemental water.
Some sites/cultivars flower outside March–June; no year-round bloom claim.

plants.name: Seaside Daisy

botanical.growthForm: Low herbaceous perennial with leafy basal/branching mound
botanical.persistence: Perennial; foliage persistence depends on climate and stress.

confidence.zones: low: conservative whole-zone 7 from -5°F tolerance; upper 10 provisional
confidence.bloomMonths: medium-high: documented April–July primary spring/summer period

caveats: Full sun/dry reflects coastal conditions; inland heat calls for light shade and more water.
Do not extrapolate coastal tolerance to hot inland/desert full-sun sites.
Fall repeat may follow pruning but should not become a guaranteed bloom window.

plants.name: Blueblossom

botanical.growthForm: Large true woody evergreen shrub; can become tree-like
botanical.lifespan: Perennial shrub; repeated hard pruning and unsuitable sites can shorten life.

confidence.dimensions: medium-high: representative upright form, wild/unpruned plants may exceed it
confidence.zones: medium: conservative overlap; rejects NC's much colder lower bound
confidence.bloomMonths: high for published mid-May–mid-June window, geography still matters
confidence.grow: planning estimate informed by rapid growth

caveats: This record represents upright blueblossom, not a creeping/prostrate selection or var. repens.
NC's USDA 5 lower bound conflicts strongly with OSU's (7)8 and cold-damage discussion; do not use it.
A 12-ft footprint is substantial. Do not imply perpetual small size through routine pruning.

plants.name: Vine Hill Manzanita

botanical.growthForm: Low spreading true woody evergreen shrub
botanical.persistence: Evergreen foliage and persistent dark reddish woody framework.
botanical.lifespan: Perennial shrub; no fixed lifespan proposed.

confidence.dimensions: high: explicit true-species grower dimensions; OSU somewhat shorter
confidence.bloomMonths: medium: winter/spring mapped to representative January–March

caveats: The true species has a narrowly restricted Sonoma origin; North American provenance must not imply statewide local nativity.
Source nursery-propagated plants; never suggest collection from the wild.
The true species prefers its native sandy, drained conditions and is not automatically as adaptable as Howard McMinn.

cultivars.name: Howard McMinn

confidence.dimensions: high: exact cultivar independently confirmed by OSU and UC

caveats: Use a distinct taller mounding preview and dimensions from the low species.
OSU 4–8 × 6–10 ft and UC 4–6 × 5–7 ft overlap around the proposed 6 × 7 ft; some mature plants become larger.
Cultivar is a named selection, not a claim of locally sourced wild provenance.

plants.name: California Coffeeberry

botanical.growthForm: True woody evergreen shrub; occasionally a small tree
botanical.persistence: Evergreen leaves and persistent woody framework.
botanical.lifespan: Perennial shrub; no fixed lifespan proposed.

confidence.dimensions: high for selected representative garden range; species very variable

caveats: Primary part-shade setting fills the understory role; species also grows in sun with an altered, often denser habit.
Some populations/selections exceed this typical garden size; do not substitute dwarf cultivar dimensions.
Use current Frangula name and searchable Rhamnus synonym; berries are ornamental/wildlife value, not a food recommendation.
